bullets.text: Q3 CR was 95.2; monthly CRs were 95.4, 97.6, and 92.4; aggregate six-month (April–September) CR reached 94.3 within a 6.2-point range.
Issued $500M in 3.75% senior debt; repurchased 22.2M shares; planned $350M debt payoff early next year; debt-to-capital remained just inside the 30% guideline.
Portfolio total return was (2.2)% amid equity volatility; pretax unrealized gains fell $434M to $871M; short duration and 25% Group I asset limit maintained.
Quarterly premium grew 4% with high state variability; Florida and New Jersey posted very good growth and profitability; New York improved; Michigan remained on the watch list.

Customers experiencing catastrophe response showed incremental policy renewal gains compared to a control group; auto weather claims achieved reasonably rapid closure, and repair capacity generally appeared sufficient for demand.
Commercial Auto written premium rose 10% in Q3 (+3% YTD with a 91.4 CR); Name your Price, Snapshot, and mobile functionality initiatives progressed as expected.

Progressive strives to maintain sufficient pricing contingency to produce targeted outcomes over reasonable timeframes. Comfort with Massachusetts new business pricing increased, and the state moved toward early maturity.
Developed a considerable inventory of new commercials within the Superstore/Flo campaign to communicate distinctive features like Name your Price and Snapshot to consumers.

Monthly combined ratios reflected other-than-normal claims frequency. Reserving challenges exist, but the short tail on auto weather claim resolution tended to mitigate longer-term concerns regarding exposure and pricing assumptions.

Progressive adjusted capital structure by adding debt and repurchasing equity amid what appeared to be depressed valuations, maintaining capital adequacy to execute underwriting plans independently of portfolio valuations.
